ranking.note: Raised from P2: a concrete data race (issue #36515) in the IPC mining interface external miners build on is a reliability/correctness defect, the strongest such item on this list.
Raised from P2: introduces BlockTemplateManager, which #33922, #36356 and #36357 all build on, in addition to removing full block assembly and cs_main acquisition on every waitNext tick.

Moved up: it is the only fix for a user-visible failure in production mining RPCs (spurious 'Internal bug detected' on longpoll shutdown, issue #34262), which outranks the refactors and tooling below it.
Moved up: template weight/sigop accounting against consensus limits is core to this category even though the per-block fee upside is tiny.
Moved up: signed-overflow UB that silently drops prioritised transactions from templates is fee-accounting correctness, ranked above tooling and test-only work despite the contrived trigger.
Moved down: valuable developer tooling and end-to-end coverage, but per the category it sits behind template-correctness fixes rather than ahead of them.
Lowered to P4: reviewers confirm the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, making this a narrow contract-consistency tidy-up.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain: #35581 introduces BlockTemplateManager; #33922 (refcounts in BlockTemplateManager), #36356 and #36357 build on it. Review #35581 first, as its design choices constrain the others.
#36356 is an explicit prerequisite of #36357 (the card says it unblocks it); they must be reviewed in that order even though #36357 carries the user-visible getmininginfo fix.

Direct conflict of approach: #36047 adds handling for createNewBlock() returning nullptr during shutdown, while #36451 makes CreateNewBlock/CreateNewTemplate return util::NotNullUniquePtr and deletes such null branches. A decision is needed on which contract holds; #36047 should be reviewed first since it fixes a reported user-facing bug (#34262).

#36525 and #35300 both change the BlockTemplate/submitSolution IPC surface (mutex guarding vs. a new 'precious' argument plus ordinal deprecation); #36525 should land first so the locking model is settled before the interface is extended.
#35598 was extracted from #33922; it is test-only and its value is contingent on the feeThreshold behaviour #33922 exercises, so it carries no independent urgency.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: two correctness/infrastructure items (#36525, #35581) that the rest of the IPC mining work depends on, a P2 block of external-miner interface capability (#35671, #33922, #35300), and a long P3 tail of small template-correctness fixes, refactors into BlockTemplateManager, and test/tooling work. Nothing here threatens template validity outright, which is why the P1 band is narrow.
